messages:
ops-alert-bot: ALERT: us-east-1 GPU pool queue depth spiked to 3.2k across serving cluster. p95 latency 1.2s, p99 4.6s. Autoscaler lagging; node restarts detected. Suggest temporary request-level controls (rate limits/quotas) while infra stabilizes.

maria: seeing it in the dashboard. thanks. any signs whether it's driver OOMs, scheduler bottleneck, or noisy tenants?

ajay: looked at node logs — 4 nodes in restart loop with nvidia-driver crash loops. Kernel OOMs on some pods. Suspect last driver rollout ~2h ago. usable GPU capacity down ~28%.

devon: with ~28% capacity loss we should blunt burstiness. propose emergency per-customer soft caps: cut QPS to ~50% for top 10 highest-util customers in us-east-1, return 429s with Retry-After. Ramp in 10% decrements every 2 minutes.

maria: +1 to gradual ramp. soft 429s so clients can backoff. also we should avoid total cut for latency-critical accounts — allowlist up to 2 tokens per account. @samir can you push policy?

samir: preparing policy now. plan: create policy emergency/us-east1/1778004321 with params: scope=customer, targets=top-10-by-qps, qps_multiplier=0.5, soft=true, allowlist=[]. Dry-run output below:

```
Dry-run: matched 11 tokens
estimated token/sec reduction: 46%
affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat
simulated 10% step ramp: OK
```

samir: running POST to admin API in 20s:

curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/ratepolicies \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"name":"emergency/us-east1/1778004321","scope":"customer","targets":"top-10","qps_multiplier":0.5,"soft":true,"ramp":{"step_pct":10,"step_secs":120}}'

deploy-bot: POLICY APPLY: emergency/us-east1/1778004321 applied to 11 tokens. ramp schedule: 10% steps every 120s. Estimated immediate token/sec reduction: 46%. Monitoring hooks: https://console.internal/dashboards/ops/gpu-us-east1

elena-cs: thx. CS on standby. I'll draft a short advisory to customers: "temporary throttling in us-east-1 due to degraded GPU capacity; we're actively mitigating; expect intermittent 429s for high-volume requests; working to restore in 1–3 hours." Which accounts should we contact directly?

clare-product: Need to whitelist a couple latency-critical customers (enterprise auth workflows). how many can we allowlist without blowing the mitigation?

maria: we can allowlist up to 2 tokens per account. keep count small. if we add allowlist entries, update the policy and re-run dry-run to ensure reduction target still met.

ajay: infra action: rolling back GPU driver rollout now. nodes are draining/rebooting; 3/4 problematic nodes are rebooting and rejoining. ETA 18–36 minutes depending on kernel hang retries. if rollback succeeds we can start relaxing caps.

devon: also initiating cross-region routing for non-stateful workloads: shift ~20% of stateless traffic from us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 to relieve pressure. command queued: `./ops/shift_traffic --from us-east-1 --to eu-west-1 --percent 20`

samir: traffic-shift job queued. monitors will alert if target region GPU util > 80% or latency increases.

elena-cs: I'll open a shared status-channel and publish an update to status.redwood.com with the advisory and ETA. CS will notify top customers A/B/C with the short message.

maria: good. I'll keep this thread updated with rollback progress and any changes to rate policy. if you see customer-facing spikes, escalate to #oncall and tag me. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: emergency/us-east1/1778004321 created by samir. incident_state=mitigating. tickets: #INC-1778, runbook ref: ops/runbooks/gpu-degraded.md

maria: closing loop for now. next update in ~5m unless something changes.
